claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Adding 5–10% aluminum or titanium to HfMoTaTiZr will reduce its density.
Adding 5–10% aluminum or titanium will maintain the alloy's room-temperature mechanical properties.
Adding 5–10% aluminum or titanium will maintain the alloy's elevated-temperature mechanical properties up to 1000 °C.
The intervention will form either a solid solution or intermetallic compounds.
The resulting solid solution or intermetallic compounds will maintain mechanical integrity.
The added aluminum or titanium will replace some heavier transition metals in the matrix.
Replacement of heavier transition metals by lighter elements will reduce the alloy's overall density.
The proposed substitution will preserve the alloy's strength.
The proposed substitution will preserve the alloy's thermal stability.
The intervention will reduce density by approximately 5–15% relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The intervention will cause no significant loss of mechanical strength at room or elevated temperature.
The intervention is expected to be effective from room temperature through 1000 °C.
The hypothesis applies to mechanical loading that does not exceed the modified alloy's yield strength.
The density reduction and retention of mechanical properties depend on alloying percentage and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The intervention describes adding 5–10% Al or Ti, whereas the mechanism requires those elements to replace heavier transition metals. The hypothesis does not specify which constituent is removed or whether the percentages describe addition, substitution, atomic percent, or weight percent.
